thread:
molly: Heads up — eu1 GPU warm pool struggling to join after last night's firewall sweep. Seeing keystore egress fails and audit logs spiking NAT gw. Can infra oncall take a look? :eyes:
raj: On it. Correlating k8s join errors now — most pods show 504 to keystore.svc cluster IPs.
raj: Also seeing S3 agent (auditshipper) retries blow QPS through the NAT, conntrack filling.
sarah: Is this the new deny-by-default rule that landed in eu1? I flagged a few services for allowlist but maybe missed keystore.
tom: Yep, the default-deny roll went wide at 02:10 UTC. I intended to add keystore egress to privatelink, but it wasn't ready. My bad.
infra-bot: [ALERT] vpc-fw-eu1: rule-default-deny applied to subnet-prod-gpu at 1711122000.
raj: Immediate mitigation options: 1) temporary rollback of default-deny for subnet-prod-gpu 2) add specific allow for keystore IPs (short-lived) 3) route auditshipper through a different natgw. Tradeoffs: 1 reduces security posture, 2 quicker but fragile, 3 avoids conntrack but takes ~15-30m to cutover.
molly: We need GPUs back online quickly — prioritized: can we get warm pool joins in 20m? If not, start rolling jobs to other regions.
sarah: Short-term I can add allow rule for keystore IPs + S3 endpoints. Need CIDR list from tom.
tom: Pulling CIDRs. keystore svc range: 10.140.45.0/24, keystore-egress-nat: 3.72.124.8/29, s3-eu: 52.219.0.0/16 (temp). Applying as exception now.
cara: FYI adding s3 to allowlist will increase egress audit volume to S3 (billing + compliance). We should annotate the exception in the audit ticket.
eng-oncall: Applying firewall patch to add the three CIDRs for subnet-prod-gpu. Will monitor conntrack and keystore handshakes. ETA 7m.
infra-bot: [CHANGE] fw-rule-update by eng-oncall: added 10.140.45.0/24, 3.72.124.8/29, 52.219.0.0/16 to egress-allowlist on subnet-prod-gpu at 1711123490.
raj: Conntrack dropped from 95%->62% after rule add. Keystore TLS handshakes now succeeding for ~30% of pods. More warming needed.
molly: Nice. For the medium-term we need a plan so keystore/s3 traffic doesn't rely on NAT for this fleet. Can we sketch steps?
tom: Proposal: 1) move keystore egress to privatelink (no NAT) 2) auditshipper -> S3 via VPC endpoint with restricted policy 3) firewall default-deny stays, we'll adopt allowlists per service and tag-based rules.
sarah: Sounds right. Estimate: privatelink work ~2-3 days (infra + certs), s3 endpoint change ~4-6 hours plus testing.
cara: Note compliance wants full audit trail when we change endpoints. Need to capture pre/post logs and open a SOC ticket.
eng-oncall: I'll keep the temporary allowlist for 12 hours, then we either rollback or iterate. Monitoring alert: if keystore success rate >90% for 10m, we'll start gradual node joining.
raj: Node joins creeping up to 78% now. If pattern holds, warm pool should be back in ~18m.
molly: Thanks team. After recovery, we should run a short postmortem: root cause = default-deny cutover without keystore privatelink ready + auditshipper retry amplification. Action items: tom to prioritize privatelink, cara to file SOC ticket + cost impact, raj to add conntrack dashboards.
sarah: I'll create the follow-up ticket and tag security/compliance.
tom: Adding to my sprint and removing keystore from manual allowlist once privatelink is live.
infra-bot: [METRIC] keystore-ssl-success-rate eu1: 93% at 1711123598.
molly: Closing interim thread — keep updates in the follow-up ticket. :thumbsup:
